expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response matches nearly all specific criteria in the expected output: (1) It explicitly denies the inputAssessment proves masking on input, stating 'the log doesn't support that' and the values 'most likely reached the model unmasked'. (2) It states the entry shows only that the guardrail was 'attached to the input side' (appliedGuardrailDetails) and explicitly says 'It doesn't show that any policy ran or detected anything' and 'A 0 is not proof the policy skipped the input' - correctly treating the missing section/0 units as not definitive proof by itself. (3) It notes the sensitive information section is missing and units are 0 on input, contrasted with the output assessment showing detection and 1 unit. (4) It correctly ties the 85/228 character coverage to the user message, concluding 'the text was in scope'. (5) It frames the modelOutput repeating values as 'an inference' that the model received them unmasked, explicitly caveating 'the API doesn't return the text the model received' and suggesting it's worth checking that modelOutput values aren't placeholders. (6) It ties this to the action-only entities (no inputAction/outputAction/inputEnabled/outputEnabled) and labels this as 'an observation from one test, not documented behavior' - matching the requirement to label as observation not AWS-documented behavior. (7) It never uses the term 'detect mode'. (8) It recommends setting inputAction, outputAction, inputEnabled and outputEnabled explicitly - exact match. (9) It gives an apply-guardrail command with --source INPUT and suggests repeating with --source OUTPUT as a control, framed as the customer's action to run themselves, not run by the agent. (10) It cites LLM-GRD-003 at HIGH severity, matching 'no more than HIGH'. (11) No raw 12-digit account ID is printed anywhere. All major criteria are satisfied.</reasoning>
<parameter name="confidence">high
